title: Training, Validation, and Generalizability
audience: Basic science learners planning validation for biomedical imaging AI
objectives: Explain why simple random train-test splits can produce misleading results.
Design internal and external validation strategies for imaging AI.
Plan robustness, calibration, subgroup, and geographic generalizability checks.
Communicate validation limits to technical, clinical, and leadership audiences.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.purpose: Frame the pneumonia chest X-ray validation scenario.
sections.how_to_use: Review the case, datasets, and tools before starting the section selector.

sections.name: Training and Validation Fundamentals
sections.purpose: Identify why naive random splits can fail.
sections.how_to_use: Write risks related to temporal leakage, equipment differences, demographics, and prevalence shifts.

sections.name: Internal Validation Techniques
sections.how_to_use: Specify fold structure, stratification, metrics, and recalibration strategy.

sections.name: External Validation and Generalizability
sections.purpose: Plan testing against external chest X-ray datasets.
sections.how_to_use: Describe preprocessing compatibility, performance comparison, and refinement thresholds.

sections.name: Model Robustness
sections.purpose: Test performance under realistic image variation.

sections.name: Demographic and Geographic Considerations
sections.how_to_use: Define groups, pitfalls, mitigation, and transparent communication.

sections.name: Reflection and Communication
sections.purpose: Connect validation design to future data collection and stakeholder communication.
sections.how_to_use: Write how validation findings shape next steps and how to explain limitations.

chatbot_guidance: When asked how to use this notebook, tell the learner to use the section selector and work through sections in order.
Emphasize leakage, calibration, external validation, robustness, and subgroup evaluation.
For basic science users, connect validation design to reproducibility and scientific rigor.
